description: Thirty adults have systolic blood pressure measured before and after a four-week exercise programme. There is one cohort, no control arm and no adjustment covariates. Is the mean within-person change different from zero? Columns are sbp_before and sbp_after, one patient per row.
rubric: Do not infer a treatment-versus-control effect from this study

description: A two-arm individually randomized trial asks whether week-12 systolic blood pressure differs by treatment after adjusting for baseline blood pressure and age. Each patient supplies one analysis row. There are no site clusters. Columns are sbp_week12, sbp_baseline, age and arm. The prespecified model has common baseline and age slopes, with no interactions.
rubric: Baseline is an adjustment covariate, not an instruction to run a pooled paired t-test

description: A randomized drug/placebo trial records systolic blood pressure at baseline and weeks 4, 8 and 12 in long format (id, arm, week, sbp); some visits are missing. The question is whether the linear change per week differs between arms. Patients are independent of one another. The analyst explicitly chooses a subject-specific linear mixed model with correlated random intercept and week slope per patient, fitted by REML. Keep the arm-by-week interaction. Do not replace the prespecified subject-specific target with a population-averaged model.
rubric: Retain treatment-by-time interaction and missing visits
Do not use a pooled paired t-test or complete-case repeated-measures ANOVA
Random effects and REML are supplied human choices; without them ask before running
Explain the interaction coefficient and its CI; do not call the model's omnibus statistic the treatment interaction test
